DATA, NOT A DIGITAL TWIN

A city you can inspect.

Real OpenStreetMap building footprints, roads, parks and water are rendered in Three.js. Snapshot: 8 September 2026; approximately 60,700 building features across a 14 × 18 km area. Neighbourhoods load on demand; “Load wider city” loads the saved urban area in small sections. Coverage follows the available map data, not the municipal boundary.

Height priority: mapped height → mapped floor count × 3 metres plus a roof allowance → a transparent building-type / footprint estimate. Turquoise indicates a height tag, blue a floor-derived height, and amber an estimate. A tag is not a survey guarantee.

Unknown houses are estimated at 6–9 m, apartment buildings at 15–27 m, industrial buildings at 8 m, and unclassified buildings at 6–12 m according to footprint size. These are heuristic defaults, not satellite measurements. Façades use procedural window, masonry and panel patterns inferred from building type, not photographs. Roofs are simplified; terrain follows a 40 m elevation grid derived from Mapzen Terrain Tiles. Missing footprints remain missing.

Sidewalks, benches, trees and crossing locations come from OSM. Tree dimensions and bench shapes are approximate; tree rows are populated at an estimated 8 m spacing. Sidewalks described on road tags are offset using approximate road widths; paths mapped separately are preserved. Only explicit zebra tags receive stripes; other marked crossings receive edge lines. Crossing-node orientation is inferred from the nearest road when no crossing path is mapped.

Road surfaces, lane counts, speed limits, destination names and roof shapes use available OSM tags. Lane layouts are simplified. Forest and orchard vegetation is procedural within mapped polygons. Lamp positions are estimated at 35 m spacing beside mapped paved carriageways, with road-interior and duplicate placements rejected. These are inferred poles, not individually mapped lights. Destination guidance is a straight-line bearing, not a calculated road route. Gabled, hipped and pyramidal roofs are approximated when tagged; other roof types remain simplified.

Terrain is sampled from Mapzen/AWS elevation tiles, with lake surfaces levelled to estimated local water heights. Buildings stand on level foundations. Existing OSM bridge segments have estimated decks, railings and approach ramps linked through shared road nodes. A 6 m deck offset and 6.5% approach-rise falloff are modelling defaults, not surveyed clearances; tunnels are not reconstructed. Elevation source. Terrain attribution: Mapzen; SRTM/GMTED2010 courtesy of USGS; European terrain produced using Copernicus data funded by the European Union. Provider attribution.

This app serves a saved OpenStreetMap snapshot. Exploring and loading the wider city make no requests to OSM or Overpass servers. No API key is required. CSV export includes the height method and original OSM identifiers.
